_comment: Labelled overlay tuning set. Built 2026-10-07 from 778 real frames clustered by the production identity notion (dhash64, hamming <= 25) into 15 DISTINCT screens, then labelled BY EYE from a contact sheet -- never from the classifier under test. Images are not committed (they live in the cold capture archive on the Pi hosts); this file is the labels plus the verdict the code gave, so the scoring is reproducible and a regression is visible.
_vocabulary: The code's own vocabulary: popup | keyboard | notification | tooltip | none | unknown. _classify_plate returns 'popup' for a centred dimmed modal; there is no 'dialog' verdict.
_populations: 778 frames -> 15 distinct screens: 11 broadcast/game CONTENT, 4 UI (console home menu, SMURFS+popup, browse UI, video+Info menu).
_result: overlay() correct on 1/15 distinct screens and 14/778 frames. On the 4 UI screens: 0/4. It answered 'tooltip' on all four, including both real dialogs.

screens.what: broadcast promo slate (station continuity slate with channel bugelogo)
console HOME MENU - a full UI screen, no overlay at all
SMURFS UI with a red 'subscription has expired' dialog - a REAL modal
video with an 'Info' context menu - raised panel, NOT dimmed

diagnosis: 'tooltip' is the degenerate fallback. A frame that produces no big plate falls through to the small-patch rule, which fires on almost anything bright-on-dark. It answered 'tooltip' on 433/778 frames and on ALL FOUR UI screens.

'popup' has never fired. Across 778 frames the verdicts were keyboard 160, tooltip 433, popup 110, notification 29, unknown 36, none 10 -- and the 110 'popup' frames are content, not the two real dialogs.

Both real dialogs fail the plate gate. Screen 6 is a 1278x280 letterboxed capture; its brightest contour is 0.315 wide x 0.800 tall, but the SMALL patches at 0.181 and 0.169 wide are the ones under OVERLAY_PLATE_MIN_W=0.25. Screen 11's candidate plates are 0.394 and 0.376 wide, so MIN_W is not what stops it -- the dimming gate is: the 'Info' menu is raised but NOT dimmed, so dim_ratio never falls below OVERLAY_DIM_RATIO=0.55 and _classify_plate returns 'ambiguous'.
keyboard/notification are not dimming-gated. Both are geometry-only (flush bottom / top-right corner), which is why broadcast promo slates and dimmed cutscenes get called keyboards and notifications.
verdict: NOT TUNABLE FROM THIS DATA. 8 thresholds cannot be fitted to 2 positive examples; any fit would be overfitting to two frames. What this set buys is the ability to PROVE the next attempt: score overlay() against these labels before and after, and never report an 'answered' rate that counts a positive overlay verdict without scoring it.
